transcript:
00:00 Jordan Kim: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood, AE on this account. Priya my SE is here as well. quick round of intros?
00:08 Mark Reynolds: Hi Mark Reynolds, Head of Platform at Pioneer. Sofia here, CTO, and Luis SRE, and Asha security.
00:16 Jordan Kim: Great. high level — you're evaluating Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private, but today we want to scope Dedicated capacity, is that right?
00:22 Sofia Alvarez: Yeah, we want dedicated reserved GPUs for prod to meet latency SLOs and also for data isolation. We also want to understand bursting and autoscale behavior, and the economics.
00:31 Priya Shah: Awesome. can you describe your current stack? where do you run inference now?
00:36 Mark Reynolds: We're doing a hybrid. Most ML models on k8s in GCP, small inference fleet on GKE, some teams self-host on prem, and we've got a small OpenAI usage for experimental features. Looking to consolidate to a predictable, cheaper path.
00:50 Priya Shah: ok, and workload? tokens per request, concurrent requests, p95 target?
00:55 Luis Ortega: Typical user flows 1.2k qps at peak across endpoints, but a lot of it is low concurrency; we have spikes to about 2.5k qps during batch jobs. P95 latency target is 300ms for the chat endpoint.
01:10 Priya Shah: Good detail. for Dedicated we usually size by peak qps and target latency; reserved GPUs give isolation and predictable throughput but you trade cost vs shared hosted. do you have requirements for cold start/burst?
01:22 Sofia Alvarez: We need bursts to handle daily ETL-style jobs and marketing campaigns; can't have those fail. We'd like auto-burst to cloud or burst pool for short windows.
01:31 Jordan Kim: Redwood Dedicated supports burst policies — you can provision reserved capacity and configure burst to a shared pool or cross-region fallbacks. bursts are billed differently and we can set caps. Priya, want to add specifics?
01:40 Priya Shah: Sure. our policy model lets you set a baseline reserved pool and a burst budget. you can also set fallback model variants with lower GPU memory or quantized versions for cheaper throughput. in practice benchmarks show 20\u201340% cost savings with quantized variants for non-critical paths.
01:55 Mark Reynolds: About isolation — we are regulated, need VPC peering, customer-managed KMS, and audit logs. We also require SOC 2 and data residency controls.
02:04 Priya Shah: Redwood Private can do on-prem or VPC-deployed Private control plane. Dedicated in a customer VPC is common — you get private networking, KMS integration, and audit trails; SOC 2 docs we can share.
02:15 Asha Patel: Do you support HSM for key storage? We need FIPS and HSM-backed key management.
02:20 Jordan Kim: Yes, we integrate with customer KMS providers and HSMs via standard APIs; we'll share the encryption/KMS whitepaper.
02:26 Luis Ortega: How about scaling — can we auto-scale GPUs? our jobs are bursty, we need the system to scale down when idle but not evict warm KV caches too aggressively.
02:36 Priya Shah: Redwood's runtime handles continuous batching and KV cache; scaling policies include a warm buffer to keep a small number of instances hot for low-latency. you can tune eviction and cache TTLs. for very spiky workloads we recommend a small hot baseline and a burst budget.
02:50 Sofia Alvarez: What's the expected latency on a 8k token sequence on an A100 or L40? and how does quantization affect quality?
03:00 Priya Shah: On 8k seq on A100 you'd expect end-to-end token latency around X — (note: some numbers may be approximations) but quantized int8/light quantization reduces GPU memory and can slightly add latency in some kernels; quality drop is task dependent, we recommend evals. we can run a benchmark using your prompt set.
03:17 Mark Reynolds: Cost — can you give a ballpark for reserved capacity pricing vs hosted?
03:22 Jordan Kim: We'll send a pricing deck. ballpark: dedicated reserved capacity is higher fixed cost but lower per-token unit cost at scale; hosted is lower upfront but variable. we'll layout sample TCO with your traffic profile.
03:34 Luis Ortega: Are there any single-tenant options for extra isolation?
03:38 Priya Shah: Yes — Dedicated pools are tenant-dedicated; we also offer Private deployments if you need full control (VPC + on-prem). you can pin model versions, and set fallbacks.
03:47 Asha Patel: Audit logs — do you capture token-level logs or only request metadata? we need to avoid storing sensitive prompt content by default.
03:55 Jordan Kim: We support configurable logging; by default we log request metadata and can opt-in to full transcripts with retention controls. you can route logs to your S3 or SIEM.
04:05 Mark Reynolds: Great. let's talk pilot. we'd like a short benchmark run with our prompts, and a canary dedicated pool for 2 weeks.
04:13 Priya Shah: Sounds good. we'll need sample prompts, traffic profile, and a test window. we'll propose instance sizing — e.g., 4x A100s to start, with 2x as warm buffer and burst to 8 for peak, depending on perf.
04:26 Jordan Kim: Next steps we'll send pricing + SOW, security pack, and Priya will send a benchmark checklist and perf run plan. can we target next Friday for the pricing doc?
04:36 Mark Reynolds: Yes, Friday works. and we'll send sample prompts by Thursday.
04:40 Jordan Kim: perfect. thanks everyone. end.
